Magician duo go global

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
When one trick went almost deadly wrong these two didn't expect what would happen next

Summary:
Magicians create illusions, they suspend reality for long enough for us to believe they are magical. It is the oldest profession in the world and we’ve seen the same tricks done over and over, but still they blow our minds.

Brenden is one of only a handful of professional mentalist in South Africa. He bends spoons, reads and controls minds. Li Lau is 1 of only 3 escapologists, or escape artists, in South Africa and the only professional side show artist, which means he does bizarre acts like eating glass and hammering nails into his head.

Brendon and Li Lau created a never before seen magic trick that had people closing their eyes in disbelief. But during a performance in Grahamstown in 2019 the trick went wrong and Li Lau was shot in the head with a bow and arrow bolt. He survived, but they vowed never to perform the trick again. Until Britain’s got talent called and asked them to enter the show and perform that very same trick on the stage in front of a massive studio audience. They agreed and their performance has been watched online by millions.
They have subsequently been invited to perform around the world at various big talent shows.

At a time where the world is so uncertain about what the future holds I thought we could do with a little magic and celebrate some South Africans that are becoming celebs around the world

Here are the links to the Britain’s Got TALENT performance
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qAMdZ59LEwo&t=34s

Link to when it went wrong
https://youtu.be/OCJ2aWETTGk

I will but then I'll have to erase your memory completely

This is actually my fave sideshow trick and one of the first ones I learnt to perform and it will be involving this sizeable nail its called human blockhead

2:37 – 3:21
The Duo first performed their crossbow stunt at the National arts festival to sold out audiences. To perform the stunt they created this contraption, there is a scale connected to a crossbow trigger, on the one side there is a dead weight and on the other side is a bottle of water slowly leaking displacing the scale, once all the water is out the trigger is activated.
Lau is trapped in the chair using multiple chains and handcuffs.
Peels job is to solve rubix cubes and add more weight to give li time to escape
Provided Brendon adds on enough weights in time, Li has just over 2 minute to free himself.

Up sound from Video – they shoot the bow and arrow into the pineapple

Li lau
we had to test that device to make sure that no external factor would ever trigger it prematurely. So when I'm sitting in front of it even though it's cocked it's ready safety set off that thing must not fire unless we want it to fire. It took us about six months just to work on it to make sure that I'm happy for the first time sitting in front of it with a lot o it was daunting.
everything runs through your mind and that's that second when you think I'm sitting in front of something that could legitimately kill me

3:54 – 4:02
The stunt was the finale of their show but after successfully performing it multiple times, on this night something went horribly wrong

Upsound – intro to the performance

4:12 – 4:53
Brendon
So that particular day with a water maybe leaked out a little bit too quickly or maybe I didn't put on a cube as fast as I usually do or maybe lee did an escape just in time.

usually I hear the thud of the bolts hitting the back chair basically
and then I just hit silence and as soon as I took off the mask I look and I just see Lee kinda lying there and I look up at the chair where usually the bolts sticking into And there was no bolt. And I looked down at Lee and he is holding his head. and that's when you get that moment of kind of woaw

Derek 4:54 – 5:13
00:17:55:24 - 00:18:00:12
So what do you remember of that moment.
Li
I remember feeling sort of pressure on my head as I ducked down. I didn't feel any pain as such I just felt something hit me.
and just immediately felt my head. I felt the arrow protruding from it.

Upsound from video – Sorry we have to ask everyone to leave

5:14 – 5:20
Lau was taken to emergency, but the bolt narrowly missed his actual skull
And he made a full recovery

5:21 - 5:31
Link: They vowed to never do this trick again. But that all changed w hen the international TV show Britain’s got talent called them with a tantalising invitation

5:32 – 6:08
Li
They wanted us to perform it and we thought there could be no bigger platfor that BGT
Derek
What was it like being on stage. To be there for BGT
you know you get up on stage there's two and a half thousand people in the audience.
you see Simon Cowell and David Walliams. it was just so surreal just to be there.
Basically most of the audience
ended up getting us like a standing ovation which we were so honoured about.
Main thing is that did Simon Cowell liked it.
you know again I can't reveal too much but I can tell you that. Simon Cowell did indeed enjoy our act.

06:09 – 6:40
Due to COVID 19 the second round of the BGT has not yet been filmed, so Peel and Lau are still waiting to find out it if they made it through. But their performance has been seen by over 5 million people online

Brendon
it has opened in kind of a lot of these doors for international marketsthere is some more tv stuff that’s popped up some usa tv stuff some European stuff yeah its amazing

6:41 – 6:53
Everybody loves magic right and now more than ever I think we could all do with a little suspension of reality! But is it all illusion or is some of what these guys are doing, for real? (Multiple Dereks)

6:53 -7:30
Derek
00:05:09:21 - 00:05:14:27
Brendon we have got visuals of you bending this fork are you really bending it or is it an illusion
Brendon
I can tell you I am a magician by trade an illusionists but the mind is that strong that it can convince another person that what you are doing is real
Li
I am sure many people will think it is quite real because some of what we do seems so impossible, but it is a stage craft and based in the real world

7:31 – 8:00
Derek :
Li we can google a lot of the tricks the illusions we see why do so many of still us still believe in magic

Li
I think even though we can look up how a trick is done. I think a lot of people choose not to because they like being in that moments of enjoying the wonder of magic
as we do as an adult a lot of people today because we have so much information on our fingertips. We know too much maybe. So magic is something where you to suspend your disbelief. I
